title: Why supermarket basil dies so fast
text:
A pot of basil from the supermarket is not one plant: it usually holds 20 to 30 seedlings sown close together.
They were grown fast in a warm greenhouse to look full on the shelf, not to last on a windowsill.
Crowded together, the seedlings compete for water and light, and most of them weaken within 2 weeks of coming home.
Overwatering makes it worse, because the dense roots stay wet and start to rot.
The fix is to split the pot: ease the root ball apart into 3 or 4 clumps and plant each in its own pot.
Split this way, the clumps usually recover within a week and keep growing for the rest of the season.
Give each pot at least 6 hours of sun, and water only when the top of the soil is dry.
